description: Create and normalize a draft multi-agent workflow without saving it. Use this before validating or committing a generated workflow. Drafts should include explicit agents, links, sharedStateKeys, artifactPolicy, and configurable properties when the user asks for a concrete workflow.

draft.description: Workflow draft object with name, summary, goal, pattern, systemInstruction, agents, and connections. Prefer explicit ADK-style drafts over fallback generation for concrete user goals. Allowed pattern values: coordinator, hierarchical, peerReview, pipeline, parallelDebate. Agent roles: rootCoordinator, planner, specialist, reviewer, toolRunner, synthesizer. Execution modes: llmInstruction, mcpTool. Connection kinds: delegation, handoff, review, sharedState, artifactFlow. Recommended artifactPolicy values: pass-latest, pass-structured, pass-summary, pass-all, allow-failed-diagnostics. Use sharedStateKeys for named artifacts such as workflowPlan, calendarList, appointmentRecords, reviewFindings, finalAnswer.
draft.name: draft

draft_json.description: Alternative JSON string representation of the workflow draft.
draft_json.name: draft_json

goal.description: High-level workflow goal used when no draft object is supplied. For concrete workflow requests, the assistant should usually construct an explicit draft instead of relying on the fallback coordinator/specialist generation.
goal.name: goal

name.description: Workflow name used when no draft object is supplied.
name.name: name

name: agent_workflow_draft_create

draft_id.description: Temporary draft identifier that can be passed to validate or commit.
draft_id.name: draft_id

valid.description: Whether the draft can be committed.
valid.name: valid
